FACT_ID: sec10-F01 | anchor: A61
Traffic laws cover everyone on the road: drivers, motorcycle and bicycle riders, and pedestrians. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F02 | anchor: A61
The Legislature changes traffic laws from time to time, so every driver should restudy the manual every few years. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F03 | anchor: A61
Speed often turns a minor mishap into a fatal one; its main danger is making collisions more severe rather than more frequent. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F04 | anchor: A61
Alabama's basic speed law says never drive faster than is reasonable for current road, weather, vehicle and personal conditions. [A61]
Why it matters: a speed under the posted limit can still break the basic speed law.
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F05 | anchor: A61
Going faster than a speed limit is prima facie evidence of unlawful speed and can get you arrested, and every limit inside a municipality is a maximum. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F06 | anchor: A61
Statutory limits apply unless a different speed zone has been set and posted on official regulatory signs. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-F07 | anchor: A62
Statutory limits are 30 miles per hour in an urban district, 35 on an unpaved road, and 45 on a county paved road unless posted. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F08 | anchor: A62
Elsewhere the statutory limit is 55 miles per hour, with 65 where posted and 70 where posted on an interstate. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F09 | anchor: A62
Where a minimum speed is posted, going slower is unlawful in normal conditions, and you must never drive so slowly that you hold up traffic. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F10 | anchor: A62
Slow down near street, highway and railroad crossings, near flags, flares or fuses on the road, and approaching hill crests and curves. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F11 | anchor: A62
At a STOP sign, stop at the marked line; with no line, before the near crosswalk; with neither, at the point nearest the cross street where you can see traffic. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F12 | anchor: A62
A second stop may be needed when something blocked your view at the first one and cross traffic is coming. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F13 | anchor: A62
Coming out of an alley, private driveway or building in a business or residence district, always stop before the sidewalk or crosswalk area. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F14 | anchor: A62
You must stop when a school patrol member holds an official flag in the STOP position. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F15 | anchor: A62
At a red light, wait for green and a clear way, though you may turn right after stopping if you are in the proper lane. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-F16 | anchor: A63
A left turn on red after stopping is allowed only from a one-way street onto a one-way street whose traffic moves right to left. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F17 | anchor: A63
Any turn on red must yield to traffic and pedestrians lawfully in the intersection and is not allowed where a sign prohibits it. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F18 | anchor: A63
Treat an intersection with a dead traffic light as a four-way stop. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F19 | anchor: A63
A flashing red signal means the same as a STOP sign. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F20 | anchor: A63
You must also stop at railroad crossings posted with STOP signs or when a flagman or device there directs, at bridges opening for boats, and when a construction flagman or police officer orders it. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F21 | anchor: A63
For an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights and siren, ahead or behind, pull to the curb or roadside and stop completely. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F22 | anchor: A63
Following or meeting a stopped school or church bus with its stop arm out and red lights flashing, stop and stay stopped until the arm folds and lights go off. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F23 | anchor: A63
That stop also applies on a four to six lane undivided highway. [A63]
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F24 | anchor: A63
No stop is needed on a divided highway of four or more lanes when the bus is in the opposing roadway, or in a roadside loading zone where pedestrians may not cross. [A63]
Why it matters: the exception needs a divided highway; on an undivided road traffic from both directions stops.
Source: [A63 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-F25 | anchor: A64
Flashing amber lights on a school bus are a pre-warning that it is about to stop to load or unload children. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec10-F26 | anchor: A64
The amber lights come on at least 300 feet before the stop in rural areas and at least 100 ft before it in municipalities. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec10-F27 | anchor: A64
Red flashing lights with the stop arm out mean the bus is loading or unloading, and drivers from either direction stop at least 20 feet from it. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec10-F28 | anchor: A64
Breaking right-of-way rules is one of the main causes of crashes; the rules rest on courtesy and common sense. [A64]
Source: [A64 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec10-F29 | anchor: A65
When two vehicles from different roads reach an uncontrolled intersection at about the same time, the one on the left yields to the one on the right. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-F30 | anchor: A65
Entering an uncontrolled intersection at an unlawful speed forfeits any right of way you would have had. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-F31 | anchor: A65
For an emergency vehicle, pull over and stop whether it is overtaking or meeting you, but clear an intersection first, and wait until it passes. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-F32 | anchor: A65
At any intersection you must stop for a blind person using a guide dog or holding out a red-tipped white cane. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-F33 | anchor: A65
A car coming from a private road or driveway must stop and yield to traffic on the public road. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-F34 | anchor: A65
At a YIELD sign facing you, slow down and stop if needed for vehicles and pedestrians lawfully crossing. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-F35 | anchor: A65
Turning left, yield to oncoming vehicles in the intersection or close enough to be an immediate hazard. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-F36 | anchor: A65
Drivers entering on a green arrow still yield to traffic lawfully using the intersection. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec10-F37 | anchor: A66
Head-on and sideswipe crashes on two-lane highways, mostly from careless passing, cause many deaths and serious injuries. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F38 | anchor: A66
Beyond the marked no-passing areas, use extreme care everywhere in darkness, poor visibility, and on roads slick from rain, snow or ice. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec10-F39 | anchor: A66
On a two-way, two-lane road you may pass on the left only if you can finish safely without exceeding the speed limit. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0066]

Glossary: basic speed law — never faster than is reasonable for conditions [A61]. Prima facie evidence — the manual's term for how a speed above the limit is treated as unlawful [A61]. Uncontrolled intersection — one without signs or signals [A65].
Memory aid: at an uncontrolled tie, the left yields to the right [A65].
